Gravity assist visualiser

A spacecraft swings past a planet. In the planet's own frame it arrives and leaves at the same speed, but in the Sun's frame it can come out much faster or slower. Switch frames to see why.

Presets:

Approach direction is the spacecraft's heading in the Sun's frame, measured from the planet's own direction of travel: 0° is the same way, −90° is straight away from the Sun, +90° is towards it. Up in the picture is towards the Sun, which is far off; the planet's orbit is curved only slightly over this short stretch, so it is drawn straight. Distances are to scale within each view, the Sun is not.

Adding the velocities

The spacecraft's velocity relative to the planet (blue) is turned like a clock hand, keeping its length. Add the planet's velocity (orange) back on and the result (yellow) can be longer or shorter than before. The white curve is the actual velocity during the flyby.
